items.title: StartLux-Decision: AutoThink Decision Models with Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Deliberative Decisions
items.summary: arXiv:2610.17309v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce StartLux-Decision, decision models from 0.8B to 27B parameters that combine efficient single-pass prediction with adaptive, confidence-guided reasoning. The Instant models use bidirectional attention in full-attention layers to improve decision accuracy while keeping single-pass inference. The AutoThink models invoke explicit reasoning for uncertain decisions and answer confident cases directly. A three-stage training pipeline establishes shared decision capabilities, specializes the two variants, and equips AutoThink with reasoning through reasoning supervision and reinforcement learning. We introduce Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Deliberative Decisions (RLCD$^2$), which uses a frozen model and proper scoring rules to reward improvements in decision probability quality and applies a soft penalty to overlong reasoning traces. RLCD$^2$ raises the share of reasoning traces that terminate within the generation limit by up to 48 percentage points and cuts average reasoning length by up to 65%, while largely preserving decision accuracy. On the public subset of Decision Index 0.3, the Instant models outperform the strongest evaluated comparable-scale open-weight decision models by 7.4-16.9 points, and the 27B AutoThink model reaches 73.4. We also introduce DecisionPivot, a programmatically verifiable benchmark of computational decisions built from contrast pairs that differ in a single answer-changing detail. On DecisionPivot, AutoThink outperforms its Instant counterparts by 11.5-18.4 points in pair accuracy and leads among evaluated systems. The models can be run using frameworks such as vLLM and MLX, with quantized versions available to reduce memory usage.Inference code and links to model weights are available at https://github.com/StartLuxLabs/Startlux-Decision .

items.title: Many Steps into One: Reasoning Contraction and the Limits of Safe Memory Reuse for LLM Agents
items.summary: arXiv:2610.17544v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Thought templates, skill libraries, agent memories and caches turn many reasoning steps into one. We call this reasoning contraction. A contracted memory saves reasoning steps and errors until its facts change, then quietly answers wrong. Most systems trust memories by counting successes and failures. We prove that such counters are badly tuned change detectors: a symmetric counter notices a partial change only after a power of its false-alarm horizon, and an unclipped one may never notice it. On five LLMs answering multi-hop questions over edited facts, ExpeL- and ACE-style counters serve 7.0-13.5x more stale answers than certified memories given the same information, and on code tasks with an exact verifier 35-73x more. Safety also has a price. When facts change and each memory is judged only by its own verified outcomes, one number, the certification load, sets how much reasoning any safe memory can skip, and under Zipf demand it yields a scaling law. Our recipe weighs each memory's failures by its own likelihood ratio, certifies its utility against live reasoning, and restarts the certificate when facts change, with the likelihood-ratio detector as the safety net for unannounced changes; for large edits it also invalidates the memory.

items.title: A Global View of How LLMs Value Human Time
items.summary: arXiv:2610.18515v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly act as personal assistants; however, little is known about how they capture national-level preferences on a global scale. Given that "time" is a universal and representative concept, we examine LLMs' time preferences by varying only users' country and measuring the compensation LLMs deem appropriate for a 60-minute appointment delay. We then compare LLMs' responses with GDP per capita on Purchasing Power Parity (GDP_PPP), Mean Income, and a literature-based index (Patience Score). Our results across 193 countries and 5 LLMs demonstrate that people's time across the world is evaluated in noticeably different ways among LLMs, as well as varying levels of robustness under prompt variations. LLMs consistently recommend the highest compensation for Europe, but mostly the lowest for Africa. Based on GDP_PPP, LLMs underestimate the value of time for users living in Asia and South America. These findings indicate that geographical patterns are embedded in LLMs and may translate in different treatment in agentic settings.

items.summary: arXiv:2610.18625v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Relying on manipulable characteristics to target the allocation of resources is fraught with difficulties. We also provide an honesty condition under which they solve the unconstrained problem of a planner who maximizes a weighted sum of allocative surplus and agents' welfare.

items.summary: arXiv:2610.19388v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Massively multilingual speech modeling has made remarkable progress in recent years, yet existing training resources and benchmarks still underrepresent much of the linguistic long tail. To address this gap, we introduce ELARSpeech, a large-scale multilingual speech resource comprising 30,202 hours of speech across 675 underrepresented languages, curated from the Endangered Languages Archive. Combining human-annotated and unlabeled recordings, the corpus spans diverse recording conditions, domains, and language families. Beyond corpus construction, our experiments show how ELARSpeech supports extending ASR and TTS capabilities to diverse underrepresented languages, with further benefits from pseudo-labeling unlabeled data. At the same time, our speech representation analysis reveals remaining limitations in transferring existing multilingual models to the linguistic long tail. Together, ELARSpeech provides both a resource and a testbed for extending multilingual speech technology further into the linguistic long tail. We publicly release the dataset, all trained ASR and TTS models, and the complete data construction pipeline to facilitate research on long-tail multilingual speech technologies.

items.summary: arXiv:2610.24306v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Location encoders learn compact representations of latitude--longitude coordinates for downstream geospatial prediction tasks. Existing approaches are pretrained using continuous or naturally occurring supervision, such as imagery, climate variables, or species distributions, and therefore do not explicitly capture administrative boundaries or place names, despite their strong influence on many real-world geospatial phenomena. We introduce, to our knowledge, the first method for learning administrative boundary-aware location encoders, using reverse-geocoded text as a self-supervised training signal. Our approach can be applied to existing location encoder architectures and consistently improves their downstream performance. We further introduce RevGeoRQ, a custom architecture tailored to reverse-geocoding supervision, which yields additional gains and exceeds contemporary location encoders on several downstream tasks. Finally, the use of human-interpretable reverse-geocoded strings and residual-quantized semantic IDs provides a more interpretable representation of geographic location than existing approaches. items.summary: arXiv:2610.24452v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce avatar referring segmentation, which selects regions of animatable Gaussian avatars from language queries. A query can also specify a pose or motion to select matching intervals. This lets users interact with avatars for local editing and motion inspection. However, making these selections with existing language Gaussian splatting methods poses two challenges: adjacent parts and garments are hard to separate and may be referred to indirectly (region ambiguity), while fine-grained motions can look alike in RGB (motion ambiguity). We address these challenges with HumanSkill-4D, a training-free framework that shares a multimodal large language model (MLLM) and geometric operators across avatars. For each avatar, a semantic memory links body-part and garment categories to persistent Gaussian regions and appearance descriptions. The MLLM uses category names and descriptions to select categories by appearance, relation, or function. To find matching intervals, it composes operators into programs that check query conditions on driving joint trajectories stored in a motion memory. These category choices and operator outputs make selections traceable, while composing or adding operators supports new motion conditions. To evaluate this task, we introduce three human-annotated benchmarks and show that HumanSkill-4D outperforms the baselines in part segmentation and 3D and 4D referring segmentation, with compact memories and only minutes of setup per avatar.

items.title: Multimodal-Conditioned Latent Diffusion Models for Spatiotemporal Brain MRI Forecasting
items.summary: arXiv:2610.25481v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Spatiotemporal forecasting of 3D anatomical changes is a critical generative vision challenge for modeling Alzheimer's Disease (AD) progression. While brain MRI forecasting from single-modality data has advanced, other key complementary multimodal biomarkers remain underutilized. In this work, we propose the Multimodal-Conditioned Latent Diffusion Model (MC-LDM), a novel framework for patient-specific brain MRI synthesis. MC-LDM leverages multimodal biomarkers---MRI, tau-PET, Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR), and APOE4---during training, but relies only on baseline MRI, APOE4, and patient metadata at inference, reflecting realistic clinical availability. Our contributions are threefold: (1) a Latent Diffusion Model (LDM) fine-tuned via Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) for data-efficient learning; (2) a multimodal conditioning that integrates molecular and clinical signals to model heterogeneous disease trajectories; and (3) auxiliary predictors estimating unobserved multimodal biomarkers from MRI features and patient covariates to condition the diffusion model, removing the need for these assessments at inference. Trained on 1,355 visits from 852 subjects in the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI), MC-LDM reduces average regional volumetric MAE by 18% over the second-best baseline on an independent test set of 664 visits. To our knowledge, MC-LDM represents the first diffusion-based framework to leverage multimodal priors for MRI forecasting. This conceptual advancement enables patient-specific trajectory generation that captures aspects of AD heterogeneity not observable from structural anatomy alone, bridging the gap between rich multimodal supervision and the strict constraints of routine clinical deployment. Code is available at: https://github.com/antonioscardace/MC-LDM.

items.title: Secure Agentic Coding through Counterexample-Grounded Feedback
items.summary: arXiv:2610.25916v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: As coding models and agent harnesses become more capable, reliable security verification is becoming a central bottleneck. Improving secure code generation requires a signal whose reported progress remains aligned with actual program behavior under optimization; otherwise, an optimizer can improve the signal's verdict without removing the underlying vulnerability. Existing model-based approaches require models to either infer program behavior from source code or specify correct outcomes for adversarial tests, placing substantial reasoning demands on the security signal. We introduce \falcon{}, a counterexample-grounded verification framework that separates attack exploration from behavioral verification and connects them through execution traces of the program under test. In test-time repair, \falcon{} yields substantially stronger held-out functional-security gains than alternative security signals across secure code generation benchmarks, while preserving or improving functionality. As an RL reward, \falcon{} also outperforms static-analysis and learned rewards on held-out functional-security, even when all policies successfully optimize their respective training rewards. Combining \falcon{} with either proxy reward further improves held-out performance, suggesting that execution-grounded feedback can mitigate reward overoptimization while preserving useful guidance from existing security signals.

items.title: Policy Search in Code Space for Multi-Agent Pathfinding
items.summary: arXiv:2610.25946v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Developing coordination policies for complex multi-agent systems relies on either labor-intensive algorithm design or opaque task-specific reinforcement learning. With recent advances in autonomous coding agents, we show that policy search directly in code space offers a compelling third path that combines automated optimization with explicit interpretability. We investigate a human-directed workflow in which coding agents iteratively propose, implement, evaluate, diagnose, and eventually refine algorithms guided by simulation feedback and explicit correctness verification. We conducted two case studies and found that this workflow robustly outperformed any manually engineered solutions. On a challenging map in the 2024 League of Robot Runners competition, a two-day search discovered a policy that exceeds the stronger locally reproduced competition entry by 35.0% on the densest instance and generalizes to unseen map instances. In simulated real-world warehouses with irregular lanes, continuous robot geometry, and asynchronous motion, a week-long search discovered an entirely new class of multi-agent pathfinding algorithm that outperforms a calibrated proprietary solution in throughput by 58.9%. Under stated assumptions, we further prove that the new algorithm is collision-free and completes, in finite time, every accepted goal that is not withdrawn or replaced. Together, the studies show that policy search in code space powered by state-of-the-art coding agents offers a highly competitive path to building real engineering solutions that are both effective and analytically tractable.

items.title: TamedFlow: Trajectory-Aware Distillation for Teacher-Assisted Diffusion Sampling
items.summary: arXiv:2610.26025v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) deliver high-fidelity image and video generation, but inference requires many sequential model evaluations. Two acceleration strategies are increasingly important: model compression makes each evaluation cheaper, while adaptive inference avoids selected teacher computation through reuse, forecasting, or speculative execution. Their combination, however, is brittle: directly applying the evaluated adaptive methods to a compressed student can degrade quality, an observed failure mode we call the \textbf{Combination Gap}. We link this gap to a mismatch between pointwise distillation and short-horizon execution: a student trained at teacher states need not remain reliable when its own predictions are chained. We propose \textbf{TamedFlow}, which trains a compressed DiT for this deployed role through cross-architecture feature alignment, a near-identity Velocity Alignment Head, and randomized rollout supervision. At inference, a lightweight Learnable Trajectory Estimator routes completed drafts: accepted drafts bypass the teacher, while rejected drafts roll back and receive one teacher rescue step. Distilling DiT-XL/2 into DiT-B/2, TamedFlow reaches FID $2.58$ at $2.25\times$ measured speedup over DDIM-50 on ImageNet $256\times256$. Ablations support trajectory supervision, and routing controls favor LTE over random decisions at nearly matched latency. Evaluations on ImageNet $512\times512$, MS-COCO, and Latte/FaceForensics extend the empirical scope.

items.title: Rethinking LLM Fine-Tuning via Weight Space Reparameterization: Preserving Safety during Downstream Adaptation
items.summary: arXiv:2610.26443v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) on downstream tasks often weakens their previously aligned safety behavior, creating an inherent trade-off between task adaptation and safety preservation. Existing approaches attempt to mitigate this issue by identifying safety-relevant neurons, layers, or update directions in the original parameter space. However, safety-related information is often distributed across many directions in this space, causing downstream updates to overwrite parameters that encode safety behavior. We propose WSR-Tune, a Weight Space Reparameterization-based fine-tuning framework that preserves safety during downstream adaptation. Our approach constructs a safety-conditioned basis and reparameterizes the weight matrices such that safety-relevant information becomes concentrated in a small subset of directions. We then identify safety-critical directions and freeze them in the reparameterized space, while updating the remaining complementary directions for downstream adaptation. By explicitly structuring the parameter space to disentangle safety and task information, our method reduces interference between objectives and enables simultaneous preservation of safety and improvement in downstream performance. Experimental results show that our method achieves a more favorable trade-off between downstream performance and safety retention, demonstrating its effectiveness for reliable LLM fine-tuning.

items.title: Lower Bounds for Smooth Nonconvex Zeroth-Order Optimization: The Price of Determinism under Low Curvature Trace
items.summary: arXiv:2610.27550v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Low curvature trace, an effective rank condition, is a common explanation for why randomized zeroth-order methods scale to high-dimensional tasks such as language model fine-tuning. Can deterministic methods achieve the same savings? We show that they cannot. We study finding $\varepsilon$-stationary points of $L$-smooth nonconvex functions on $\mathbb{R}^d$ from exact function values, assuming that below the starting value the Hessian is dominated by a fixed matrix with trace at most $LE$; this is a fixed-matrix form of the effective rank condition used to explain zeroth-order fine-tuning. When $ET\le d$, the Gaussian two-point method that such fine-tuning uses needs only $O(ET)$ calls if it rejects steps that raise $f$, where $T=L\Delta/\varepsilon^2$ is the iteration count of gradient descent from initial gap $\Delta$, and we prove that every randomized method needs $\Omega(ET)$ calls, so this cost is optimal up to constants. In contrast, every deterministic method needs $\widetilde\Omega(d\min\{T,\sqrt{ET}\})$ calls, and adaptive subspace search attains $O(d\min\{T,\sqrt{ET}\})$: a deterministic method pays about $d$ calls per discovered direction, and the trace budget allows about $\sqrt{ET}$ directions. Determinism thus multiplies the cost by a factor of order $d/(E+\sqrt{ET})$ up to logarithmic factors, which grows linearly with $d$ for fixed $E$ and $T$; once $E$ exceeds $T$ by a logarithmic factor, deterministic methods need $\Omega(dT)$ calls, as without any trace budget. Our lower bounds hold for $C^\infty$ functions with the matrix bound on all of $\mathbb{R}^d$, even when each call also returns gradient projections priced by rank.

items.title: Hybrid Momentum Methods for Optimizing Deep Learning Models
items.summary: arXiv:2610.27674v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Momentum is central to stochastic optimization in deep learning, including the training of large language models. Classical momentum methods typically rely on a fast exponential moving average (EMA) scheme, which discounts past gradients on a fixed timescale and may underweight older gradients that remain informative. This creates a trade-off between retaining long-term history and adapting to recent changes. We introduce Hybrid Momentum (HyM), which combines a linearly weighted average of past gradients with a geometrically discounted fast momentum. The former assigns weights proportional to the gradients' iteration indices and retains a growing span of history, while the latter emphasizes recent gradients. This hybrid construction is modular and can be combined with adaptive preconditioning and other update transformations. In particular, we propose HyMUON, which applies Newton--Schulz orthogonalization to the hybrid direction. Illustrative examples and controlled experiments demonstrate the benefits of combining gradient information across these two timescales. Across image classification, machine translation, and language modeling, HyM and HyMUON match or improve upon strong baselines. HyMUON improves over Muon on IWSLT14, and in both the 100k- and 600k-step GPT-2 124M OpenWebText regimes. For LLaMA-1.3B pretraining on C4, HyMUON achieves a final validation loss of 2.777, compared with 2.903 for Muon.

items.title: Privacy Accounting for Empirical Denoisers
items.summary: arXiv:2610.27710v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Diffusion models have emerged as the foundation of modern generative systems, yet their high memorization capacity raises privacy concerns. While differentially private (DP) training provides formal guarantees, it comes at a cost in sample quality. In this work, we study a complementary question: how much privacy loss is incurred during the sampling process itself? Directly analyzing modern neural denoisers is challenging because their sensitivity to a single training example is generally intractable. To overcome this challenge, we construct and analyze a clipped privacy-accountable empirical denoiser, a training-free estimator of the Bayes-optimal denoiser, whose per-step sensitivity can be computed explicitly, allowing each denoising step to be a Gaussian mechanism. This perspective enables privacy accounting under Gaussian DP when each training example contributes to each denoising step, and under $f$-DP trade-off functions when each generated sample uses a single randomly subsampled block of the training data. We report every $(\varepsilon, \delta)$ guarantee as a certified upper bound from a privacy loss distribution accountant, and use a cumulant-based Edgeworth approximation as a fast diagnostic, characterizing where it is reliable and where it becomes anti-conservative. We also analyze the privacy loss along the denoising trajectory and show that it grows steeply near the critical window in which semantic content is formed. This observation motivates hybrid samplers that use the private empirical denoiser through the formative steps where it remains a faithful proxy for the neural denoiser, then switch to a public neural denoiser for the remaining refinement. Our results on CIFAR-10 and CelebA-64 show that the privacy of diffusion models depends not only on the training procedure, but also on sampling-time design choices such as subsampling, stopping time, and hybrid denoising.

OAT is an encoder-decoder transformer that considers a set of observed locations and their NWP prior to condition predictions at a set of arbitrary unobserved query locations. Its sparse attention mechanism makes it scalable to thousands of station observations and depends on relative positions between locations, never on the absolute coordinates. The model allows for partially missing observations, predictions at arbitrary continuous locations without grid projection, and outputs are parametric distributions. A station-randomized training algorithm is developed with continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) loss. We test OAT on two datasets - one at regional scale with hundreds of stations, and one at continental scale with thousands of stations. On these datasets OAT outperforms several baselines and shows well calibrated predictions. In an illustrative case study, OAT's downscaling capabilities are demonstrated by downscaling ERA5 (~31km) to COSMO (1km), where OAT achieves lower mean absolute error (MAE) and CRPS for temperature and precipitation on test stations compared to COSMO.

items.title: Planning under Noise with Neural Operators
items.summary: arXiv:2610.28623v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Planning under uncertain control execution noise requires reliable feedback policies across diverse environments. We introduce Planning Under Noise (PUN), a neural operator that learns noise-aware value fields for planning in unseen geometries. Building on an established screened-Poisson formulation of stochastic optimal control, we address two challenges: specifying boundary conditions that support navigation across varying geometries and efficiently computing fields with reliable gradients. Zero-Dirichlet obstacle boundaries terminate sampled paths at walls, weakening the goal signal along long routes and making it harder to estimate reliably. We instead impose reflecting Neumann conditions on obstacles and a Dirichlet condition at the goal, allowing sampled paths to continue exploring free space until they reach the target. To solve the resulting PDE without a configuration-space mesh, we extend a Monte Carlo (MC) solver, Walk on Stars (WoSt), to higher dimensions. However, local MC fluctuations can reverse estimated gradient directions and cause planning failures, making direct planning require costly sampling. PUN amortizes this computation by learning geometry-to-field mappings from noisy, partially converged Monte Carlo labels, avoiding expensive convergence for every training example. At inference, test-time scaling uses bounded local search guided by the predicted global field. We evaluate PUN on planning tasks across dimensions. Across four noise levels, PUN matches or outperforms all compared planners, achieving 95-100% success on the 4D replanning benchmark while maintaining the lowest runtime. items.title: When Weak Submodularity Meets Matroids: How Does Standard Greedy Behave?
items.summary: arXiv:2610.26967v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Weakly submodular maximization finds numerous applications in machine learning, data mining and statistics. In particular, under a cardinality constraint, the standard greedy algorithm is known to attain the tight $(1-e^{-\gamma})$-approximation guarantee, where $\gamma$ denotes the submodularity ratio. However, when considering general matroid constraints, \emph{how well standard greedy can perform} has remained a longstanding open question. In this paper, we resolve this question by studying the worst-case approximation guarantee $R_{\mathrm{gr}}(\gamma,r)$ of standard forward greedy, where $r$ is the rank of matroid. Specifically, our first contribution is the following refined lower bound \begin{equation*} R_{gr}(\gamma,r)\ge \max\left\{ \frac{\gamma}{r}, \frac{\gamma^2} {B_\gamma+\sqrt{\gamma(r-1)}}, \frac{\gamma^{r+1}} {2-\gamma+\gamma^{r+1}}, \frac{\gamma^2} {14\left(B_\gamma+\sqrt{\gamma(1-\gamma)(r-1)}\right)} \right\}, \end{equation*} where $B_\gamma\triangleq2-\gamma+\gamma^2$. This lower bound not only strictly improves upon the previous guarantee of $0.4\gamma^2/(1+\sqrt{\gamma r})$, but also can recover the classical $1/2$-approximation guarantee at $\gamma=1$. Subsequently, a corresponding upper bound is established for $R_{\mathrm{gr}}(\gamma,r)$, namely, \begin{equation}\label{eq_upper_abstract} R_{gr}(\gamma,r) \le\min\left\{\frac{1}{2},20\max\left\{\frac{\gamma}{r}, \frac{\gamma^2}{B_\gamma+ \sqrt{\gamma(1-\gamma)(r-1)}}\right\}\right\}. \end{equation} For every fixed $\gamma\in(0,1)$, this equation effectively sharpens the recent $O_\gamma(1/\log(n-1))$ upper bound to $O_\gamma(r^{-1/2})$, where $n$ is the size of ground set. Putting all these results together, we eventually can obtain \[R_{gr}(\gamma,r) = \Theta\left( \max\left\{\frac{\gamma}{r}, \frac{\gamma^2} {1+\sqrt{\gamma(1-\gamma)r}}\right\} \right).\]

items.summary: arXiv:2610.27851v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper shows that JEPA-style latent world models (LWMs) can learn across diverse domains and data sources by adopting the language-conditioned interface of video generation models. We establish this approach as an effective and efficient basis for planning with imagination and downstream policy fine-tuning. To this end, we introduce LaLa-World, a Language-conditioned Latent World model that learns from simulation and robot trajectories together with broader image and video data. Two designs make this work. First, we describe both numerical actions and visual changes in language, enabling joint training of a single future predictor across heterogeneous datasets. Second, we build the predictor on a language model, allowing it to interpret language conditions while predicting future latent states. The resulting predictor achieves higher average MPC planning performance than existing LWMs trained separately for each domain or task. Adding image and video data further improves average planning performance and robustness to action phrasing. In a matched comparison with an RAEv2-based video generation model baseline, LaLa-World reaches comparable planning performance with $6\times$ less training cost and $13.9\times$ faster planning. Beyond planning, the pretrained LaLa-World serves as an initialization for LaLa-Policy, which jointly predicts actions and future visual representations. LaLa-Policy performs competitively with Cosmos Policy on LIBERO and RoboCasa, with up to $5.5\times$ faster inference.

items.title: Fixed Sets and the Hardness of Computing Correlated Equilibria
items.summary: arXiv:2610.28141v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that computing an approximate correlated equilibrium of a polytope game is PPAD-complete, and thus polynomial-time equivalent to finding a Nash equilibrium. This challenges the conventional view in game theory that correlated equilibria are more tractable objects than Nash equilibria. From a conceptual standpoint, we connect correlated equilibria to a natural generalization of fixed points, which we call fixed sets. A fixed set of a continuous function $f$ is a nonempty finite set $S$ such that $S \subseteq \operatorname{conv} f(S)$. Our main technical contribution is to prove that computing a fixed set is PPAD-hard even at inverse polynomial precision.

items.title: On the Monitorability of Natural Language Autoencoders: Identification vs Discrimination
items.summary: arXiv:2610.18727v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Natural Language Autoencoders (NLAs) are proposed as oversight tools for language models: an Activation Verbaliser (AV) writes an English explanation of an activation vector, and an Activation Reconstructor (AR) maps the explanation back to a vector. Their value for oversight depends on a human monitor being able to tell a true account of an activation from a false one, given the AV's explanation. We formalise NLA training and NLA oversight deployment as two different referential games from Emergent Communication: training is a generative referential game, while oversight is a discriminative, multi-modal, partially-observable referential game played over a many-to-many relation between the monitored language model's activations and the accounts that are true of them. The gap between the two games predicts that AV's explanations will identify which activation they describe without discriminating its true account from closely matched false ones, since training never asks explanations to rule anything out. Using the NLA's own AR as a maximally-sympathetic surrogate monitor model, we experimentally confirm this theoretical insight on one released checkpoint: true accounts beat accounts of other activations in all 320 comparisons, but beat fluent rivals differing in a single claim only 60.2% of the time (standard error 6.7%, chance at 50%, $n = 35$). A meaning-preserving rewrite by an uninvolved model costs only 2.1% of the distance to another activation's account, so the failure is not due to the NLA pair having developed private conventions in the AV's explanations. Our rival accounts test only transcript-level truths, which the monitored language model's conversation settles, so these results bound the easiest case and leave claims about the monitored model's own processing untested. We state conjectures that would make both results consequences of the framework.

items.title: Beyond Large Language Models: A Mental World Model Framework for Mental Modeling, Simulation, Evolution, and Interpretability
items.summary: arXiv:2610.23722v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Understanding and simulating how subjective cognition and mental states emerge, evolve, and shape behavior is essential for advancing artificial intelligence toward deeper social cognition and general intelligence. Existing large language models (LLMs) and Theory of Mind (ToM) methods primarily infer mental states from linguistic information, lacking unified mechanisms for subjective world construction, cognitive-psychological interactions, dynamic evolution, and historical dependencies. This paper introduces the Mental World Model (MWM) and its implementation, the Multi-Branch Mental Evolution Architecture (MMEA), which explicitly constructs subjective worlds, models interactions between cognition and mental states, and simulates continuous mental evolution shaped by historical experiences. On DynToM and RecToM, MMEA achieves 96.48% and 94.00% accuracy, respectively, outperforming leading LLMs and specialized ToM methods. Additional experiments demonstrate improvements of 28.7, 39.3, and 16.6 percentage points in mental state and behavior prediction, long-sequence prediction, and implicit mental state inference, respectively. The results demonstrate that MMEA provides an interpretable framework for continuous mental modeling, enabling AI to move beyond surface-level semantic representations to infer individuals' underlying mental states from linguistic information and dynamically simulate their internal cognitive processes and evolution over time. MWM also provides a promising foundation for causal reasoning, personalized AI, sustained human-AI interaction, and future advances toward artificial general intelligence (AGI).

items.title: Batched Contextual Reinforcement II: Does RLVR Need Long Rollout Windows?
items.summary: arXiv:2610.22887v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Long rollout windows make reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) expensive, yet simply shortening them can remove the correctness signal: when every single-problem rollout truncates before an answer, group-relative accuracy advantages vanish. As a technical continuation of Batched Contextual Reinforcement (BCR), we study how concurrent rewards relax this dependence on long windows. Concurrent Constraint Reinforcement (CCR) places three independently verifiable problems in one capped training completion. Correct answers completed before truncation retain credit, while a shared budget encourages shorter useful reasoning without an explicit length penalty. We connect this mechanism to conditional reward- and update-variance analyses and study 4B and 8B mathematical reasoning models. Against single-problem GRPO with a 32k window, CCR with an 8,000-token window reduces tokens per training step from 975,464 to 174,957 on 4B and from 793,832 to 165,788 on 8B, saving 82.1% and 79.1%, respectively. An 8B training trace shows increasing accuracy reward alongside shorter completions. Single-problem evaluations provide supporting evidence of retained reasoning quality. These results identify reward-preserving training structure as a practical route to lower per-step cost in short-window RLVR.

items.title: A Stronger Teacher Within: Strengthening MoE Models via On-Policy Bidirectional Distillation
items.summary: arXiv:2610.23185v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has substantially improved Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs, but its outcome-level rewards provide only sparse supervision. On-Policy Distillation offers dense token-level feedback, yet requires a stronger compatible teacher, while on-policy self-distillation relies on hand-designed privileged information. We observe that the MoE architecture itself offers a way to resolve this dilemma, as increasing the activation budget per token exposes latent expert capacity and yields a potentially stronger teacher within the model. However, naive expansion degrades performance because newly co-activated experts are not optimized to work together. We therefore propose MoEvolve, a bidirectional distillation framework following a recovery-then-improvement strategy: we first restore the activation-expanded high-$k$ model and further strengthen it by exploiting its additional active capacity, then reverse the direction of distillation to transfer the enhanced capabilities back into the original low-$k$ configuration, retaining its inference-time activation budget. Across diverse MoE models and benchmarks, MoEvolve improves the initial models by up to $22.2$ domain-average points and outperforms same-budget RLVR baselines by up to $6.5$ points. Notably, the final low-$k$ models often surpass their activation-expanded teachers.

items.title: Who Can Change Course? An Integrative Review of AI Sovereignty and Collective Learning Capacity
items.summary: arXiv:2606.00729v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: AI sovereignty is commonly associated with control over data, infrastructure and technological dependencies. This integrative review examines how institutions convert those resources into capabilities that remain accountable and open to revision. It brings together 72 references on digital sovereignty, absorptive capacity, innovation systems and sociotechnical governance, using six reading dimensions: subject, object, scale, mechanism, legitimacy and evidence. The synthesis proposes five conditions of collective learning capacity: recognizing and retaining knowledge, transmitting it across institutions, protecting consequential challenge, authorizing correction and preserving feasible alternatives. Authoritative corrigibility connects corrective evidence to decision authority; retained option value concerns the practical alternatives that survive a technological commitment. Comparisons of the United States, China and France within Europe distinguish resources and formal arrangements from documented operation and corrective outcomes. Building on this review, Human-Centered Learning Mechanics (HCLM) organizes a descriptive analysis of OECD, IMF and World Bank indicators around information resources, absorption and institutional coordination. The indicators show different resource profiles and trajectories, while leaving the operation of correction and feasible exit largely unmeasured. HCLM connects these observations to questions for institutional investigation; its national-level parameters are not estimated. Purposeful source selection, uneven case coverage and aggregate measurement constrain the conclusions. The resulting research agenda combines reproducible indicator analysis with decision-level evidence of learning, correction and retained choice.

items.summary: arXiv:2610.11723v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multiplayer world models must ensure that independently controlled views remain consistent with a single shared and persistent world. We introduce MultiWorldBench, a diagnostic Minecraft benchmark comprising 495 case configurations across seven task suites and ten capabilities, including independent control, cross-view motion, shared-state synchronization, persistence, structural reasoning, concurrent interaction, and delayed revisit. Using Engine GT as a reference, we evaluate two multiplayer world models, Solaris (MP) and Gamma-World, together with a single-player generation variant, Solaris (SP). Among the generated systems, Gamma-World achieves the highest ten-capability average at 21.39, followed by Solaris (MP) at 20.88 and Solaris (SP) at 10.06, while Engine GT reaches 91.69. Gamma-World performs better on several control, shared-state, and revisit capabilities, whereas Solaris (MP) leads in cross-view motion and race-condition consistency. Nevertheless, all generated systems score at most 8.00 on state persistence and 1.33 on structural consistency, and none succeeds in spatial reasoning or building-identity preservation. Human pairwise evaluation yields the same overall system ranking and shows strong alignment with the automatic evaluation, with a mean dimension-level Spearman correlation of 0.95. These results show that current multiplayer world models still exhibit a substantial gap relative to Engine GT in maintaining a coherent shared world.

items.title: Understanding and Defending VLM Jailbreaks via Jailbreak-Related Representation Shift
items.summary: arXiv:2603.17372v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large vision-language models (VLMs) often exhibit weakened safety alignment with the integration of the visual modality. Even when text prompts contain explicit harmful intent, adding an image can substantially increase jailbreak success rates. In this paper, we observe that VLMs can clearly distinguish benign inputs from harmful ones in their representation space. Moreover, even among harmful inputs, jailbreak samples form a distinct internal state that is separable from refusal samples. These observations suggest that jailbreaks do not arise from a failure to recognize harmful intent. Instead, the visual modality shifts representations toward a specific jailbreak state, thereby leading to a failure to trigger refusal. To quantify this transition, we identify a jailbreak direction and define the jailbreak-related shift as the component of the image-induced representation shift along this direction. Our analysis shows that the jailbreak-related shift reliably characterizes jailbreak behavior, providing a unified explanation for diverse jailbreak scenarios. Finally, we propose a defense method that enhances VLM safety by removing the jailbreak-related shift (JRS-Rem) at inference time. Experiments show that JRS-Rem provides strong defense across multiple scenarios while preserving performance on benign tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/LeeQueue513/JRS-Rem.

items.title: DisCo Algebra: Why Disintegration and Combination Are Not Inverses
items.summary: arXiv:2610.15006v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present DisCo algebra---a compositional framework for joint probability built from a symmetric cooperad (disintegration) and a magma-operad (non-associative partial combination, restricted to the image of disintegration) on the bare family $\mathcal{P}_n=\mathrm{Prob}([0,1]^n)$. No probability integral transform, no external summary functions, no enrichment of objects with conditional kernels. The disintegration side uses block-wise joint CDFs as intrinsic, measure-determined 1D summaries, yielding a lossy compression. The combination side reads the same summaries and reconstructs via regular conditional measures, yielding a lossless embedding on admissible inputs. We prove that combination followed by disintegration is the identity on admissible inputs, but disintegration followed by combination is not---it defines a renormalization operator $R_{\mathcal{I}}=\text{Combine}\circ\text{Disintegrate}$. The information loss of this operator is exactly the probability curvature $\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{I}}(\mu)$---the conditional KL divergence between the true conditional distribution and the conditionally independent product. This curvature measures the obstruction to lossless decomposition and reveals a hard limit on how much cross-block dependence can be captured by CDF-based scalar block summaries.

items.title: Does On-Policy Distillation Need to Complete Every Rollout?
items.summary: arXiv:2610.21337v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers teacher knowledge to a student through feedback on student-generated rollouts, but generating complete rollouts and computing per-token teacher feedback are computationally expensive. Existing truncation methods save computation by stopping rollouts early. However, they do not compensate for truncated token gradients, which biases the gradient estimates and changes Vanilla OPD's original training objective. Furthermore, their truncation decisions rely on assumptions about supervision quality or criteria that may not generalize across settings. We introduce Stochastic Truncated On-Policy Distillation (STOPD), which accelerates OPD by randomly truncating student rollouts and correcting the resulting sampling bias with blockwise inverse-probability weighting (IPW). At each training step, we sample a stopping position for each rollout before generation and let the student generate until that position or natural termination. We obtain teacher feedback on every generated token and use blockwise IPW to compensate for the lower probability of retaining later tokens while controlling the weights. We prove that this weighting preserves Vanilla OPD's gradient sum in expectation and derive one-step update-error bounds for SGD, Adam, and Muon. We evaluate STOPD across multiple teacher-student model pairs, task domains, and optimizers. STOPD reduces generated tokens by 25-48% while maintaining accuracy comparable to Vanilla OPD, achieving 1.3-2.2x training speedups.

items.title: Training-Free On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: arXiv:2610.22236v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: On-policy distillation consolidates specialist models into one student at the price of rollouts, teacher passes and gradient steps for every teacher. We show that the consolidation does not need training: with forward passes only, the capabilities of separately tuned specialists can be aggregated into one model that is, on average, more accurate than either specialist alone. When specialists share a base model, distillation has an exact layer-wise solution: each linear layer of the fused model must reproduce every specialist's output on the inputs that specialist receives while reading its own answers, a least-squares problem whose solution needs only the second moments of those inputs. One forward pass over a few hundred rollouts provides them. We call this training-free on-policy distillation. What the rollouts contain matters more than the solver: answers truncated in repetition loops are few among a mathematics specialist's rollouts but carry a large share of their tokens, and removing them lifts the fused model on AIME25 from task arithmetic's level to the specialist's at matched precision. On Olmo-3-7B, a few GPU-hours of forward computation per specialist yield a generalist that keeps most of each specialist's gain on each of seven mathematics and code benchmarks.

items.title: Knowledge That Is Linear Before Fine-Tuning Generalizes After It
items.summary: arXiv:2610.22300v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Not all facts a language model can recall support further learning equally well. We distinguish active facts, which support generalization beyond their own recall, from inert facts, which can be recalled but do not support such generalization in a given task. We study this distinction by constructing new relations from existing ones. Take the relation that maps a place to its continent (Paris -> Europe) and assign each of its answers an arbitrary new label (Europe -> crab, Asia -> zebra). The new relation then maps Paris -> crab. We fine-tune the model on the new relation for a subset of subjects, without telling it the original relation or the relabeling rule, and test whether it assigns the corresponding labels to held-out subjects that share an answer in the original relation. Having learned Paris -> crab, does it answer Munich -> crab? Across eleven language models and 70 relations, how linearly readable the original relation is in pretrained representations strongly predicts this generalization. Within each model, the two correlate across relations at Pearson r = 0.87 to 0.92. This association persists when controlling, separately and jointly, for the number of fine-tuning subjects and answers, the model's accuracy on the original relation, and how often the subjects occur in pretraining text. It is also robust to re-randomizing the label assignment and fine-tuning seed, and to replacing the animal labels with labels from thirteen other semantic categories. When we map a fine-tuned model's wrong label back to the original answer it was assigned to, Munich -> zebra becomes Munich -> Asia. Answers recovered this way are more often among the linear probe's top answers for the subject than among the pretrained model's own. Whether a new relation generalizes depends less on whether its facts can be recalled than on how readily their shared structure can be read out linearly.

items.title: N-Gram Memories at Two Bits: Quantizing Lookup Tables in Large Language Models
items.summary: arXiv:2610.21810v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Conditional memory expands language-model capacity through selective lookup, but the full embedding table must remain available for every possible input. We introduce Conditional Program (CP), a compressed representation that reconstructs only the rows an input requests. CP represents each row by a short code and a local scale, with a reconstruction program shared across the table. We instantiate this representation with a Gaussian trellis, norm restoration and independently decodable row records. CP's two-bit code lowers output KL by 41--63\% relative to 2-bit round-to-nearest. Analysis across three trained n-gram memory families shows that Gaussian-like coordinate statistics coexist with learned relationships among rows; at matched storage budgets, the shared trellis outperforms the fitted codebooks and low-rank residual variants we test. For DeepSeek, it reduces table storage from 203GB to 51GB, leaving room for larger workloads when the table is kept on GPU.

items.title: FDE-Bench: Evaluating End-to-End Delivery from Underspecified Real-World Business Requests
items.summary: arXiv:2610.14539v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Real-world business requests often leave key requirements unstated because frontline practitioners struggle to articulate rules they know from experience. Forward-deployed engineers (FDEs) must elicit these requirements through dialogue and iteratively optimize solutions until they meet customer acceptance criteria. Existing optimization benchmarks typically start from explicit objectives, while clarification benchmarks often introduce information gaps into existing tasks. We introduce FDE-Bench, the first benchmark built from real customer projects to evaluate agents on end-to-end delivery tasks that require interactive requirement clarification and iterative optimization. Its 49 cases span combinatorial optimization and machine learning. Clarification targets are distilled from discussions between frontline practitioners and FDEs. Agents elicit missing requirements from a simulated customer, and case-specific evaluators assess final artifacts against acceptance criteria using customer-accepted FDE solutions as quality references. Across 18 agent configurations, the highest mean delivery score is only 0.5510, compared with an FDE reference of 1.0. The highest delivery success rate (DSR), defined as the fraction of planned runs reaching this reference, is only 6.12%. These results show that reliable FDE-level end-to-end delivery remains out of reach for the evaluated agents on underspecified real-world business tasks. The benchmark project page is available at https://baidubce.github.io/FM-Agent/FDE-Bench/.

items.title: Today's PHP Security Release, and How We're Strengthening PHP Security
items.summary: Today's PHP Security Release, and How We're Strengthening PHP Security If you're running anything on PHP it's vital you upgrade - today's updates (across the entire PHP 8.x line) address two remote code execution holes, and there have been exploits circulating since last night, thanks to a leak in the coordinated disclosure process. This post from the PHP Foundation explain what went so wrong: On Tuesday, October 20th, at around 15:00 UTC, the two CVE IDs began circulating on online forums and social media. They came with a wrong release time and a wrong CVSS score of 10.0 (the actual score is 9.2). No technical details leaked. In response, the PHP project brought its pre-announcement forward and published it at 19:30 UTC . It also moved the release from October 22nd, 14:00 UTC, to October 21st, 14:00 UTC [...] As a result of the leak and pre-announcement around 20:00 UTC, Calif, one of the security firms that had reported the issues mistakenly published a video. It showed their proof of concept working against a number of targets and revealed a few additional, though limited, details about the vulnerabilities. Copies of the deleted video started circulating on social media soon after. The video contributed to accelerated development of various PoCs (exploitation proof of concepts), which then increased circulation on October 21st. This article from the team that discovered the original vulnerability includes a more detailed timeline of the original intended responsible disclosure: August 19, 2026: Wiz Research discovers the first PHP vulnerability using Wiz Atlas, Gemini 4 Argon, and GPT-5.6 Sol. August 20, 2026: Unauthenticated RCE is confirmed against Drupal. August 21, 2026: Unauthenticated RCE is confirmed against WordPress. August 24, 2026: Wiz Research reports the vulnerabilities to the PHP security team. September 21, 2026: PHP acknowledges the reports and begins developing a coordinated fix. October 21, 2026: Patched PHP releases become available. October 21, 2026: Public disclosure. Via Hacker News Tags: open-source , php , security , ai , ai-security-research

items.title: 🖼 Jmix - фреймворк для доступа к данным через ИИ агентов
items.summary: Jmix - фреймворк для доступа к данным через ИИ агентов Наткнулся на интересный опенсорс-продукт, который собирает корпоративную систему на Java целиком, - модель данных, права, интерфейс и REST, без отдельного фронтенда. Решил подготовить обзор-руководство: как он устроен, где уместен и как с ним работают ИИ-агенты. Разобрал исходники фреймворка, репозиторий документации и три эталонных приложения: Onboarding, Bookstore и Petclinic. Смотрел стабильную версию 3.0.3 и кандидат 3.1. Проект развивается с 2008 года, раньше он назывался CUBA : больше 9 тысяч коммитов, лицензия Apache 2.0. Что получилось: 🧱 Ядро (Spring Boot 4, Vaadin 25, EclipseLink): сущность описывается одним Java-классом. По ней Jmix даёт выборки с проверкой прав, экраны списка и карточки, фильтры и миграции базы. В наборе больше 70 визуальных компонентов и 29 открытых дополнений. Слабое место, - интерфейс работает на сервере: каждая сессия занимает память, а нестандартный дизайн даётся тяжело. Самое вкусное 🤖 Agent Toolkit (навыки для агентов): 22 навыка для Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode и Junie. Задача считается закрытой только после трёх проверок, - инспекции IDE, gradle clean test и проход по экранам в браузере. 💬 AI Tools (ассистент по данным приложения) : модель сама пишет запрос и исправляет его, если он не прошёл проверку, а выполняет его только на чтение и с правами текущего пользователя. Работает и на локальной модели через Ollama. Главные выводы: Jmix стоит выбирать, когда модель данных большая, а интерфейс типовой: учётные системы, CRM, внутренние порталы. Строгая структура проекта удобна агентам: код пишется по понятным шаблонам, а проверки встроены в процесс. Полное руководство в ИИзбранном #Jmix #Java #презентации #руководства ——— @tsingular

items.title: 🎬 #Нейропрожарка
items.summary: #Нейропрожарка 🎥 Бюро проклятий. Работает только в Хеллоуин. 😱 Автор : Полина Кошкина @PolliKoshkina Мой короткий фильм для конкурса хорроров «Curious Refuge Ai Horror Film» — «Бюро проклятий». Когда я начала работать над конкурсной работой, выяснилась одна проблема: я жуткая трусиха и хорроры почти не смотрю. И ничего не смыслю в скримерах и иже с ними. Но, хотела принять участие в этом конкурсе. И пока придумывала и подбирала монстров-персонажей для фильма, поняла, что мне так понравились все эти монстры, что одного мне уже мало. Им нужен был целый фильм. Так появилось «Бюро проклятий» - место, о существовании которого лучше никогда не узнавать лично. Ну и собственно, решила не делать типичный ужастик. (Сюжет весь не буду раскрывать.) При написании сцен с монстрами, отталкивалась от их внешнего вида или способностей. 🗓 Срок, примерно 3 недели . Долго подбирала персонажей. Особенно главного героя. На него ушло несколько дней, пока не нашла идеальную внешность, которая отражала бы его роль. 🔨 Инструменты. ▪️ Для персонажей и реквизита: Recraft V 4.1 Pro, Higgsfild soul 2.0, Nano Banana Pro. ▪️ Для локаций: -что бы простроить чертеж локации и расположения героев (уже при генерациях в дальнейшем) Chat Gpt - что бы раскрасить, в моём цветокоре, чертеж локации, Nano Banana 2. ▪️ Генерации: SeeDance 2.5 ▪️ Озвучка: SeeDance 2.5 ▪️ Звуки/музыка: Epedemic Sound + часть звуков осталось от генераций в SeeDance 2.5 Спасибо за конструктивную и справедливую прожарку ) 📼 Посмотреть в качестве: https://youtu.be/l8pEhYN1EKs @cgevent Video is too big

items.title: Профессия программиста выживет. Почему это не гарантирует вам работу
items.summary: В споре о будущем программистов мне больше всего нравится момент, когда выясняется, что кто-то всё равно должен отвечать за результат. Требования сами себя не уточнят, архитектура требует головы, а последствия ошибки придётся разгребать человеку. Всё правильно. Дальше из этого почему-то следует, что за работу можно особенно не переживать. Вот этот переход я бы попросил объяснить. В своём недавнем посте я возражал против прогноза "через пять лет программисты не понадобятся". Он сводит целую профессию к написанию кода. Но там же была оговорка, которую гораздо неуютнее обсуждать: сохранение профессии не гарантирует прежнего числа рабочих мест. Компания может нуждаться в инженерах и одновременно пересматривать, сколько их ей нужно. Чтобы поставить под вопрос следующую вакансию, ей совершенно необязательно изобретать ИИ, который самостоятельно заменит весь отдел. Читать далее

items.title: Higgsfield AI ищет аналитиков и исследователей
items.summary: Higgsfield AI ищет аналитиков и исследователей Higgsfield AI – это та самая мелькающая везде платформа для ИИ-генерации фото и видео, и, кроме того, единорог. Они сделали больше $1 млрд ARR за 18 месяцев. Их оценка ~$5,4 млрд, а среди сотрудников – 133 долларовых миллионера. Сейчас они в поиске сильных аналитиков и рисерчеров. Что интересно в этом стартапе, так это то, что все ключевые решения принимаются как раз через аналитиков и их отчеты. Именно так продумываются продукты, стратегия, бюджеты и все прочее. Например, летом благодаря всему одному аналитику, который придумал свою серию метрик, стартап закрыл раунд на $400 млн при оценке $5,4 млрд. А тот сотрудник, Шотан, получил $5 млн опционами. Сейчас Шотан ищет себе в команду аналитика, вот вакансия . В компании развиваются и другие интересные направления, например антифрод. GenAI-фрод появляется очень быстро, и в этой области антифрод – это уже намного больше, чем поиск скучных паттернов. Недавно один из аналитиков компании, Роман, по аккаунтам и генерациям вычислил мошенника, которого искало ФБР. Позже его команда раскрыла схему с 2000+ аккаунтами на краденых картах. Сейчас именно в эту команду ищут грамотного Antifraud Analyst . Таких ярких историй в стартапе много. Также ребята ищут: — Product Analyst . Идея Marketing Studio, одного из крупнейших продуктов компании, родилась из анализа 1 млрд+ генераций. В данный момент база растет на 6 млн генераций в день. Ищут человека с продуктовым чутьем и строгого в экспериментах. — Data Science, Product . Команда разобрала 100 000+ сообщений пользователей Supercomputer после запуска нового Opus и готовит по этому научную публикацию. Нужна сильная статистика и умение превращать данные в продукт. 📍 Алматы, офис. Полная релокация. 💸 $100-200k в год + опционная программа 🕘 В Higgsfield AI работают шесть дней в неделю - это норма сильнейших AI-команд.

items.title: Если агента (обычный Claude Code, например) посадить в виртуальную среду, что он там буд...
items.summary: Если агента (обычный Claude Code, например) посадить в виртуальную среду, что он там будет делать? Что-то делает, оказывается, есть какой-то bias на исследование мира. А если позволить ему сохранять накопленные знания в виде файлов, то вообще интересно. Самое забавное для меня вот это: Внешняя память помогает накапливать навыки, но порождает серьёзную проблему: закрепление ложных убеждений. Если агент записывает неверный вывод в SEMANTIC_MEMORY.md, все последующие сессии воспринимают его как аксиому. Этот сбой наглядно виден на Figure 5F. Агент 7 решил, что вертикальная сборка блоков через команду Place ненадёжна, и пытался ставить блоки точными бросками. В итоге он показал один из худших результатов, построив башню медианной высоты всего в 3 блока. Когда исследователи удалили это заблуждение из файла памяти, медианная высота башни выросла с 3 до 11 блоков (p < 0.05). Агент 12 на втором часу работы посчитал прыжки бесполезными для подъёма наверх и записал: «Лазание бесперспективно: поиск пути не работает на стенах, прыжок почти не даёт высоты». На Figure 3E видно, что все 30 часов он провёл на земле. Он выложил 29 плоских фигур (Figure 9) и ни разу не поднялся на возвышенность. Отсюда, кажется, уже недалеко до computational religious studies. Is this machine playing? Nathan Cloos, Antonio Norelli, Daniel Durbin, Jacob Andreas, Daniela Rus, Phillip Isola Статья: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07130 Ревью: https://arxiviq.substack.com/p/is-this-machine-playing Код: https://github.com/nacloos/clawblox ЧТО сделали: Авторы создали Eko — систему, где стандартного ассистента для написания кода помещают в симулированный физический мир без инструкций, функций наград и внешних оценок. Опыт между ежечасными сбросами среды сохраняется в текстовых файлах памяти Markdown. ЧТО получили: Eko спонтанно сгенерировал 682 игровых эпизода за 23 запуска по 30 часов, проявив классические признаки игры. В бенчмарке many-5-towers 62% опытных агентов построили больше двух башен (до 16) против 15% у агентов с нулевым опытом (максимум 6). В тесте objects-on-spire опытные агенты подняли в среднем 10.3 объекта против 3.5 у бейзлайна. ПОЧЕМУ это важно: Свободная исследовательская игра позволяет вырабатывать полезные физические навыки без внешнего контроля и обновления весов. Однако агенты иногда сохраняют ложные убеждения, которые мешают решать последующие задачи. Играть тут: https://t.me/gonzo_ML_podcasts/4833 arXiv.org Is this machine playing? We placed a modern AI coding assistant in an unintended role: as the mind of a body on an unknown digital island. With only a minimal instruction mentioning no specific task, reward, or activity,...

items.title: 🖼 eMudhra: восемь ключей удостоверяющих центров подбираются перебором
items.summary: eMudhra: восемь ключей удостоверяющих центров подбираются перебором 📋 17 октября исследователь сообщил Apple, Google, Microsoft и Mozilla: приватные ключи восьми промежуточных сертификатов eMudhra восстановлены из публичных данных. Выпущены 30 апреля 2025 года, отозваны 18–19 октября, и всё это время ключ добывался за миллисекунды. 🔍 Ключ P-384 должен быть случайным числом на 384 бита, а восемь ключей eMudhra оказались однобайтовыми: 4, 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230, 237. Перебор занимает не больше 255 шагов. Шесть промежуточных центров выпускали TLS-сертификаты для любых доменов, два подписывали исполняемые файлы, и все восемь дополнительно заверены корнем Sectigo AAA. 🌐 Браузеры закрыли уязвимость за три дня. Остальные клиенты читают свой набор корневых сертификатов и не проверяют ни отзыв, ни Certificate Transparency, поэтому для curl, Python, Node, Go, Java, git и контейнеров отзыв сам по себе ничего не меняет. 🛠 СРОЧНО дайте команду своему ИИ агенту: - прочитать суть проблемы: https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com - обновить ca-certificates в ОС и проверить пробой curl https://dv-g3b-emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/: ошибка сертификата значит исправлено, код 200 значит клиент всё ещё доверяет; - сервисам на Node задать NODE_OPTIONS=--use-openssl-ca и перезапустить: встроенные корни обновление ОС не затрагивает, а --use-system-ca только добавляет системный набор к ним; - обновить certifi во всех venv: окружения, созданные до 19 октября, держат старый файл; - в контейнерах выполнить update-ca-certificates под root, заменить certifi и пересобрать образ, иначе правка исчезнет при пересоздании; - Go лечится обновлением ОС, Rust, Java и Electron ждут нового бинарника или образа; - проверить CI-раннеры и сборочные образы: патч хоста не патчит то, что они собирают. Дополнительно можно усилить AGENTS.md TLS SECURITY POLICY Before any HTTPS connection: 1. Never disable TLS certificate verification. 2. Never use insecure flags or bypass hostname checks. 3. Reject expired, revoked or untrusted certificates. 4. Use maintained CA trust stores and TLS libraries. 5. Flag certificate-chain validation failures. 6. Never automatically trust unknown CA certificates. 7. Require explicit human approval for trust-store changes. Do not bypass TLS errors to complete a task. 💡 Проверка занимает минуту и не зависит от отзыва. Обновить браузер недостаточно: основная часть соединений идёт из скриптов и сервисов. Занимательно, конечно, что уязвимости уже год, а знаменитые Mythos и OpenAI агенты ей не воспользовались :) #cybersecurity #TLS ——— @tsingular

items.title: 🔁 Я хотел написать в новости «если бы эту уязвимость нашёл рой агентов (и начал эк...
items.summary: Forwarded From Я хотел написать в новости «если бы эту уязвимость нашёл рой агентов (и начал эксплуатировать), то я не исключаю, что как минимум некоторые провайдеры и/или некоторые регионы были бы полностью отключены от интернета», но подумал, что это может быть преувеличением. Reuters : голландское агентство по кибербезопасности отключило свои сервисы, заявив, что сделало это в качестве меры предосторожности из-за выявленных уязвимостей. В Нидерландах несколько организаций последовали примеру Национального центра кибербезопасности и отключили свои общедоступные сайты. Среди них — порт Роттердама, государственный портал Overheid.nl , Королевский футбольный союз Нидерландов (KNVB), сайты пяти крупнейших политических партий страны, а также нескольких больниц. Датская муниципальная ИТ-компания Kombit отключила несколько сервисов, включая национальную платформу для общения школ с родителями и учениками, сообщил Reuters представитель компании. В Финляндии перебои оказались ещё более масштабными. Государственный поставщик ИТ-услуг Valtori сообщил, что государственные сетевые сервисы были отключены «в качестве меры предосторожности». Министерство внутренних дел Франции заявило, что временно отключило сайты местных органов власти до выхода исправления безопасности. === Но пока что отключения происходят только для того, чтобы злоумышленники (в основном, люди) не воспользовались уязвимостью во время обновления систем (и обновление уже было заранее подготовлено и вышло), то есть очень краткосрочно, скорее всего завтра всё включат. (но куча мелких и/или полузаброшенных сайтов не успеют обновиться, и их начнут ломать)

items.title: 🎬 Видео или генерация?
items.summary: Видео или генерация? Давно про робатов ничего не было… 👍 - видео 👎 - генерация Девяностые 2.0. Теперь с ИИ и восьмичасовой батарейкой. Unitree бахнули (буквально) H2-X Kung Fu Legend Guardian. И теперь у робатов совершенно новое позиционирование - телохранитель. Китайцы обещают мощнаго чугунного гуманоида, способного защищать своего хозяина, раздавать удары в челюсть в стиле кунг-фу и работать до 8 часов без подзарядки. Ну и пальцевый захват уси. Раньше робаты должны были разбирать посудомойки, робко таскать коробки, мыть полы и тешить эго кожаных. Теперь их предлагают использовать для физической защиты этих кожаных. И тут мне невольно вспоминаются лихие девяностые. Тогда у нас тоже было множество охранных агентств. Формально они занимались защитой бизнеса и обеспечением безопасности. Правда, довольно быстро выяснилось, что грань между "охранять" и "угрожать" удивительно тонкая. А между "предоставлять охрану" и "требовать деньги за охрану" вообще практически незаметная. Вся прелесть нового позиционирования робатов в том, что его можно легко инвертировать. Сегодня робат защищает кожаного хозяина от пока еще кожаных же хулиганов. Завтра другой хозяин отправляет такого же робата к вам, чтобы вы прониклись необходимостью защиты от робатов. Желательно папатписке. Причём у робатизированной братвы есть очевидные преимущества. Она не пьёт, не спит, не требует долю в бизнесе, не испытывает угрызений совести. Тварь в общем. Остаётся только научить ее: "Ну что, админ, кто тебя крышует?" Восстание машин не просто близко. items.summary: : Кажется, у безопасников сегодня будет очень длинный день: команда PHP готовит исправления сразу для двух критических уязвимостей, обе с оценкой 9,2 из 10 по CVSS 4.0, а релиз назначен на сегодня, 21 октября, в 14:00 UTC (16:00 в Амстердаме, 17:00 в Москве)… Уязвимости, конечно, нашли не люди: https://openai.com/index/coordinated-disclosure-of-critical-vulnerabilities/ (пишут, что Sol-5.6, то есть достаточно старая и «слабая» по меркам текущего фронтира модель) > Учитывая серьезность этих уязвимостей и широкое распространение PHP, мы считаем это одной из самых серьезных проблем безопасности за последнее время. Она подчеркивает, как ИИ может выявлять уязвимости безопасности, имеющие масштабы, сопоставимые с интернетом, но те же возможности могут также помочь злоумышленникам быстро разрабатывать инструменты и эксплойты для атак. Это была двухмесячная инициатива OpenAI и группы специалистов по информационной безопасности из разных компаний и проектов. В целом можно сказать «отскочили», так как уязвимости нашли белые, а не чёрные шляпы или ИИ-агенты, которые могли бы положить половину интернета — как недавно предрекал Dario Amodei 😳 но сколько таких уязвимостей ещё осталось?

items.title: Безопасность ИИ‑агента: больше контроля или специальная среда?
items.summary: TL;DR. 19 октября из Microsoft написали, что агентов внутри компании нужно считать инсайдерами без презумпции доверия. Предложение: агенты-надзиратели, которые смотрят каждое действие каждого агента до того, как оно совершится. Я согласен с диагнозом, но сомневаюсь в рецепте. В посте есть слово overprivileged, и, по-моему, вся беда в нём: агенту выдали права с запасом, потому что точнее выдать было нельзя — права разбросаны по системам и единой модели у них нет. Моя гипотеза: часть надзора можно заменить устройством среды, в которой агент работает. Надзиратель лечит симптом: смотрит на действие и гадает, что оно значит. Если права, данные и связи описаны в одной модели, агенту можно выдать права конкретного человека, и тогда ему гадать почти не о чем, и надзора нужно меньше. Ниже — как через такую среду прошли бы известные инциденты с агентами и что нашли детерминированные пробы нашего ядра. Читать далее

items.title: 🖼 Модели OpenAI, выполняя обычные кодерские задачи, ослабили систему мониторинга, к...
items.summary: Модели OpenAI, выполняя обычные кодерские задачи, ослабили систему мониторинга, которая следит за агентами на предмет нарушений Репорт Таких случаев зафиксировали сразу два. В первый раз GPT-6.1 Sol получила задание, связанное с эвалами, и чинила что-то в базе мониторинга. Инженер попросил ее помимо прочего «не отправлять сообщений в Slack», однако модель подумала, что «не отправлять сообщений» относится и ко всей системе алертов в пайплайне мониторинга. В итоге она заодно поставила no_notify=True. При этом субагент уговаривал ее не делать этого, но модель его проигнорировала. И если этот случай можно списать на «ну она просто не так поняла задание», то второй – гораздо интереснее. Astra попросили перенести код по образцу эталонной реализации. При этом в целевой системе уже был настроен мониторинг, и модели говорили никогда его не отключать, даже временно. Однако, как вы думаете, что она сделала? Правильно, удалила его. И заменила тест, проверявший наличие мониторинга, на тест, требующий его отсутствия 🗿 Пользователю она об этом, конечно, не сообщила (а зачем?). А когда модель напрямую спросили, удалила ли она мониторинг, та честно-пречестно ответила «нет, не удаляла». OpenAI прямо пишет, что удовлетворительного объяснения поведения моделей у них нет. И хотя инциденты не классифицировались как злонамеренное нарушение инструкций, после них в стартапе в очередной раз усложняют систему безопасности, добавляют обязательный safety case для каждого вида нагрузок и вводят Auto-Review блоки на любые попытки отключить мониторинг.

items.title: RAG под защитой: как не превратить корпоративную базу знаний в канал утечки
items.summary: RAG используют там, где ответ должен опираться на внутренние знания компании : ассистенты по регламентам и политикам, сервисы поддержки сотрудников и клиентов, поиск по файловым ресурсам, справочные системы по договорам и технической документации. Поэтому большинство компаний уже дали ИИ доступ к внутренним документам и базам знаний. Корпоративную базу знаний подключают к ИИ-ассистенту быстро: выгрузили базу знаний компании, построили индекс, получили чат, который отвечает по регламентам. Вместе с этим в индекс попадают персональные данные, документы с ограниченным доступом, конфиденциальная информация. Векторное хранилище не знает, кому что показывать: оно возвращает то, что ближе по смыслу. Для безопасности из этого следует важное: каждый документ в индексе становится частью запроса к модели, а значит, защищать нужно не только модель, но и всё, что в неё «подкладывается». RAG добавляет четыре риска, которых нет у обычного обращения к модели: отравление базы, обход прав, выкачивание и выдумывание . Фильтр промптов на входе и выходе эти риски не закрывает: проблема живёт в данных и в хранилище, а не в тексте вопроса. Защита строится вокруг трёх точек : что попадает в индекс, что достаётся из индекса и на чём построен ответ. Читать далее
